Package com.falkordb

Class FalkorDB.Builder

java.lang.Object
com.falkordb.FalkorDB.Builder
Enclosing class:
FalkorDB
public static final class FalkorDB.Builder extends Object
A fluent builder for a Driver, created via FalkorDB.builder().

All options are optional; unset options fall back to the fixed defaults documented on each setter (localhost:6379, no credentials, no TLS), never to the environment FalkorDB.driver() consults. Instances are not thread-safe and are intended to be configured and built on a single thread. Validation happens in build().

      public FalkorDB.Builder database(int database)
      Selects the database (default 0), as the path of a redis://host:port/2 URI does.

      A Redis Cluster has a single database, so a non-zero index is rejected by build() with cluster(String...), and when the first connection finds the endpoint is a cluster. The connections to Sentinels never select one; only the master's do.

    • ssl

      public FalkorDB.Builder ssl(boolean ssl)
      Enables or disables TLS. Unset, TLS is on when sslContext, sslParameters or sslHostnameVerifier is set, and off otherwise.

      ssl(true) alone uses the JVM's default trust store and verifies the server's hostname. ssl(false) together with one of the settings above is a contradiction, which build() rejects.

      Parameters:
      ssl - whether to connect over TLS
      Returns:
      this builder

    • sslContext

      public FalkorDB.Builder sslContext(@Nullable SSLContext sslContext)
      Connects over TLS with sockets from this SSLContext, which carries the trust material that authenticates the server and, for mutual TLS, the key material that authenticates the client. Setting it turns TLS on. Unset, the JVM default applies. 
      
 KeyStore trustStore = KeyStore.getInstance("PKCS12");
 try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(Paths.get("truststore.p12"))) {
     trustStore.load(in, trustStorePassword);
 }
 TrustManagerFactory tmf = TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm());
 tmf.init(trustStore);
 SSLContext context = SSLContext.getInstance("TLS");
 context.init(null, tmf.getTrustManagers(), null);

 Driver driver = FalkorDB.builder().host("db.example.com").port(6380).sslContext(context).build();

      The same TLS settings are used for every connection the driver opens: to the server, to each Redis Cluster node, to the Sentinels and to the master they name. Cluster nodes and Sentinel masters are usually reported by IP address, so for hostname verification to pass their certificates need IP subject alternative names.

      Parameters:
      sslContext - the context to create TLS sockets from, or null to clear it
      Returns:
      this builder

    • sslParameters

      public FalkorDB.Builder sslParameters(@Nullable SSLParameters sslParameters)
      Applies these SSLParameters to every TLS socket: protocols, cipher suites, SNI server names and the endpoint identification algorithm, which decides whether the server's hostname is verified. Setting them turns TLS on. Unset, the defaults apply, which verify the hostname.

      They are used as given, and new SSLParameters() has no endpoint identification algorithm, which would mean no hostname verification. build() therefore rejects parameters without one unless an sslHostnameVerifier does the checking: call setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS") to verify the hostname, or setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("") to skip that check deliberately. 

      
 SSLParameters parameters = new SSLParameters();
 parameters.setProtocols(new String[] {"TLSv1.2"}); // TLS 1.3 needs Java 8u261 or later
 parameters.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS");
 Driver driver = FalkorDB.builder().host("db.example.com").sslParameters(parameters).build();

      build() keeps a copy, so changing the object afterwards has no effect on the driver.

      Parameters:
      sslParameters - the parameters for each TLS socket, or null to clear them
      Returns:
      this builder

    • sslHostnameVerifier

      public FalkorDB.Builder sslHostnameVerifier(@Nullable HostnameVerifier sslHostnameVerifier)
      Checks the server's identity with this HostnameVerifier once each TLS handshake has completed, and refuses the connection if it returns false. Setting it turns TLS on.

      It runs in addition to the endpoint identification of the parameters, not instead of it. For a verifier more lenient than the standard "HTTPS" check to take effect, set the parameters' endpoint identification algorithm to "" as well.

      Parameters:
      sslHostnameVerifier - the extra check, or null to clear it
      Returns:
      this builder

    • poolMinIdle

      public FalkorDB.Builder poolMinIdle(int poolMinIdle)
      Sets how many idle connections the pool keeps open, ready for use (default 0).

      A background task tops the pool up every 30 seconds, starting 30 seconds after the driver's first use, since the pool is created then; building the driver still opens no connection. Opening one waits at most the socket timeout, or 2 seconds when none is set, for each reply of the connection setup, so a server that accepts connections but never answers can't hold up the task. With a Redis Cluster it applies to each node's pool separately.

      Parameters:
      poolMinIdle - idle connections to keep; must be non-negative and no greater than the pool's maxIdle
      Returns:
      this builder

    • poolTestOnBorrow

      public FalkorDB.Builder poolTestOnBorrow(boolean poolTestOnBorrow)
      Checks each connection with a PING before handing it out, and replaces one that fails (default false).

      It catches a connection the server or the network closed while it sat in the pool before a query is sent on it, at the cost of one extra round-trip every time a connection is borrowed: at least once per graph call, and again each time a Redis Cluster redirect is retried. poolTestWhileIdle(boolean) catches most of the same connections in the background instead.

      The PING waits at most the socket timeout, or 2 seconds when none is set.

      Parameters:
      poolTestOnBorrow - whether to check a connection before each use
      Returns:
      this builder

    • poolTestWhileIdle

      public FalkorDB.Builder poolTestWhileIdle(boolean poolTestWhileIdle)
      Checks idle connections with a PING in the background every 30 seconds, and closes the ones that fail (default false), so that a connection the server or the network dropped while idle, for example after the server's idle timeout or a load balancer's, is not handed to a query. A closed connection is replaced when the pool next needs one, or straight away when that brings the pool below poolMinIdle(int).

      The PING waits at most the socket timeout, or 2 seconds when none is set. Idle connections are never closed merely for having been idle; poolMaxIdle(int) bounds how many are kept. The first check runs 30 seconds after the driver's first use. With a Redis Cluster it applies to each node's pool separately.

      Parameters:
      poolTestWhileIdle - whether to check idle connections in the background
      Returns:
      this builder

    • socketTimeout

      public FalkorDB.Builder socketTimeout(Duration socketTimeout)
      Sets the socket (read) timeout (default Duration.ZERO = no read deadline, so a long-running server query is never cut off client-side).

      It limits how long each read of a reply waits for data, including the reply to a query sent with a timeout, such as Graph.query(String, long): that timeout limits how long the server runs the query, not how long the client waits. The server sends nothing until a query has finished, so a socket timeout shorter than the query's ends the wait first, though the server may still run the query to the end.

      Parameters:
      socketTimeout - read timeout; must not be negative
      Returns:
      this builder

    • sentinel

      public FalkorDB.Builder sentinel(String masterName, String... sentinels)
      Connects through a Redis Sentinel deployment, naming the monitored master explicitly.

      Use this when auto-detection is not enough: it lists every Sentinel rather than a single seed, so the driver can still find the master when one Sentinel is down, and it names the master, so it works with a Sentinel monitoring more than one. Setting it makes host(String) and port(int) irrelevant — the master's address comes from the Sentinels — and suppresses probing entirely. 

      
 Driver driver = FalkorDB.builder()
     .sentinel("mymaster", "sentinel-a:26379", "sentinel-b:26379", "sentinel-c:26379")
     .credentials("user", "password")
     .build();
      Parameters:
      masterName - name of the monitored master, as given to sentinel monitor
      sentinels - the Sentinel endpoints in host:port form; at least one is required
      Returns:
      this builder

    • autoDetectSentinel

      public FalkorDB.Builder autoDetectSentinel(boolean autoDetectSentinel)
      Enables or disables Sentinel auto-detection (default true).

      When enabled, the driver probes the configured host/port once with INFO server the first time it is used; if that endpoint is a Sentinel, the driver resolves the single master it monitors and connects to that instead, following failovers from then on. This mirrors falkordb-py, falkordb-go and falkordb-ts, so the same address works across FalkorDB clients. Like every other connection, the probe happens on first use rather than in build(), which performs no I/O.

      The probe is best-effort and costs one round-trip: an endpoint that cannot be reached, or that refuses INFO, simply yields an ordinary direct connection whose failure surfaces on first use — the behaviour of every release before Sentinel support. Switch this off to skip the probe altogether when you know you are not talking to a Sentinel. It is ignored when sentinel(String, String...) named a deployment explicitly.

      Parameters:
      autoDetectSentinel - whether to probe the endpoint for Sentinel mode
      Returns:
      this builder

    • autoDetectCluster

      public FalkorDB.Builder autoDetectCluster(boolean autoDetectCluster)
      Enables or disables Redis Cluster auto-detection (default true).

      When enabled, the driver probes the configured host/port once with INFO server the first time it is used; if that endpoint reports redis_mode:cluster (or server_mode:cluster, as Valkey does), the driver learns the cluster's topology from it and sends every graph command to the node that owns the graph, so the same address works for a standalone server and a cluster. This mirrors falkordb-py. Like every other connection, the probe happens on first use rather than in build(), which performs no I/O.

      In cluster mode:

      • a graph lives on a single node, chosen by hashing its name, so queries, pipelines and transactions on one graph are served by that node. Copying a graph needs both names in the same hash slot, which a hash tag arranges ({social}-a and {social}-b); otherwise the server answers CROSSSLOT;
      • Driver.listGraphs() returns the graphs of every primary, and the server-wide commands (udfLoad, udfDelete, udfFlush, configSet) run on every primary;
      • pool sizing and connection checks apply to each node separately, and the connection settings are used for every node, so all nodes must accept the same credentials and TLS settings;
      • a cluster has a single database, so a database index, in a URI or set with database(int), is not supported;
      • when the cluster reshards or fails over, the driver follows the redirect and retries the command, up to three attempts.

      The probe is best-effort and costs one round-trip: an endpoint that cannot be reached, or that refuses INFO, simply yields an ordinary direct connection. Switch this off to skip the probe altogether. It is ignored when cluster(String...) named the nodes explicitly.

      Parameters:
      autoDetectCluster - whether to probe the endpoint for cluster mode
      Returns:
      this builder

    • schemaHash

      public FalkorDB.Builder schemaHash(boolean schemaHash)
      Sets whether queries send the hash of the schema names the client has cached (default true).

      Compact replies name labels, relationship types and property keys by number, and a graph that is deleted and recreated, by this client or any other, reuses the numbers for other names. With the hash, FalkorDB 6.2 and later add the graph's current names to a reply whenever the cached ones are stale, so every reply is decoded with the right names, and the client never has to ask for them separately. Older servers ignore the hash, and a client connected to one fetches names it doesn't have, as before; until then, a name it cached before such a recreation can still be decoded in place of the new one.

      Switch it off only if something between the client and the server rejects the extra SCHEMA_HASH argument; the client then decodes every reply as it does with an older server.

      Parameters:
      schemaHash - whether queries send the schema hash
      Returns:
      this builder

    • cluster

      public FalkorDB.Builder cluster(String... startupNodes)
      Connects to a Redis Cluster through the given startup nodes, without probing.

      Use this when auto-detection is not enough: it lists several nodes rather than a single seed, so the driver can still learn the topology when one of them is down. Only some of the nodes need to be reachable. The host and port set on this builder are ignored. See autoDetectCluster(boolean) for how a driver behaves in cluster mode. 

      
 Driver driver = FalkorDB.builder()
     .cluster("node-a:6379", "node-b:6379", "node-c:6379")
     .build();
      Parameters:
      startupNodes - the cluster nodes in host:port form; at least one is required
      Returns:
      this builder
